post_text: A federal agency has 20 working days under the Freedom of Information Act, the federal records law, to decide on a records request, and unusual circumstances can add up to 10 more. The days are the law’s limit; our systems atlas records that agencies often take weeks or months (Issue I013, “Public records arrive too late to be useful”). FOIA.gov’s page “How do I make a FOIA request?” shows where to send yours.
